native_result.query: In what context does the gardening pathway for introducing non-native plants show different prevalence styles across habitat types?
native_result.HypoA: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats.
native_result.HypoB: The gardening pathway shows different prevalence styles across habitat types: a dominant, occupancy-rich style in humanized/lowland/wet habitats (Urban, Riparian, Wetlands, Coastal; ~30-56% of records, ~36-50% of plots) versus a near-absent/incidental style in natural high-elevation forests/scrublands/rock outcrops (<=7 records, <7% plot occupancy), a contrast that persists after adjusting for elevation and land-use covariates, is opposite to the unintentional pathway's urban+cropland style, is corroborated by gardening species' narrow-to-intermediate niche breadth (0.45 vs 0.75) with a few wide-ranging ornamentals (Robinia, Dysphania, Oxalis, Araujia, Lonicera = ~42% of occupancy), and is temporally anchored in gardening becoming the dominant pathway only after 1985-2019 (75% of introductions; youngest mean residence time ~85 yr).
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) habitat x pathway contingency, chi-square/Fisher with sparse-habitat lumping, pairwise z-tests; 2) covariate-adjusted Poisson/NB (n_gard and n_unint) and logistic plot-occupancy models with RR/OR effect sizes and a habitat-only vs adjusted confounding check; 3) species-level pathway trait comparisons (Kruskal-Wallis/Mann-Whitney) + wide-ranging gardener contribution; 4) temporal surge linked to habitat pattern via mean residence time; 5) synthesis with sparse-habitat caveat throughout.

sub_hypo.text: Gardening introductions show a dominant, occupancy-rich pattern in Urban, Riparian, Wetlands and Coastal habitats, versus a near-absent or incidental pattern in natural high-elevation forests, scrublands and rock outcrops.
sub_hypo.context: Non-native plants in Barcelona province, comparing humanized/lowland/wet habitats with natural high-elevation habitats; sparse habitats are lumped where needed and interpreted cautiously.
sub_hypo.relations: Gardening accounts for approximately 30–56% of records and occurs in approximately 36–50% of plots in Urban, Riparian, Wetlands and Coastal habitats, versus at most 7 records and less than 7% plot occupancy in natural high-elevation forests, scrublands and rock outcrops. Plot occupancy is derived from gardening presence.

sub_hypo.text: The habitat contrast in gardening prevalence persists after adjustment for elevation and land-use covariates.
sub_hypo.context: Non-native plants in sampled plots in Barcelona province, with a sparse-habitat caveat.
sub_hypo.relations: Habitat differences in gardening counts and derived plot occupancy remain after covariate adjustment, assessed using Poisson/negative-binomial and logistic models with RR/OR effect sizes and habitat-only versus adjusted comparisons. The specific land-use years and buffer sizes selected for adjustment are not specified.

sub_hypo.text: Gardening's habitat prevalence pattern contrasts with the unintentional pathway's urban-and-cropland pattern.
sub_hypo.context: Pathway-specific invasion across habitats in Barcelona province, with sparse habitats interpreted cautiously.
sub_hypo.relations: Gardening is prevalent in Urban, Riparian, Wetlands and Coastal habitats, whereas unintentional introductions exhibit an urban-and-cropland style; pathway differences are compared through habitat contingency analyses and covariate-adjusted count and occupancy models.

sub_hypo.text: Gardening species have narrow-to-intermediate invaded niche breadth, while a few wide-ranging ornamentals contribute approximately 42% of gardening occupancy.
sub_hypo.context: Species-level comparisons of non-native plants invading Barcelona province, particularly gardening species and the named ornamentals Robinia, Dysphania, Oxalis, Araujia and Lonicera.
sub_hypo.relations: Gardening species' niche breadth is approximately 0.45 versus a comparison value of 0.75, corroborating habitat concentration; the comparator for 0.75 is not explicitly identified. Robinia, Dysphania, Oxalis, Araujia and Lonicera together account for approximately 42% of occupancy.

sub_hypo.text: Gardening's present habitat pattern is temporally anchored in its recent rise to dominance and its species' comparatively young mean residence time.
sub_hypo.context: Temporal introduction pathways of non-native flora in Catalonia, linked through species residence times to invasion patterns in Barcelona province.
sub_hypo.relations: Gardening becomes dominant only in the recent 1985–2019 period, accounting for approximately 75% of introductions, and has the youngest mean residence time, approximately 85 years. The workflow links this temporal surge to the habitat pattern through mean residence time.
